items.title: Lillie Delk Christian Interview, 1961-04-25
items.q: when Bottoms opened that place, he had the orchestra out there, out in, uh, Robbins, Illinois. It was called the Casino Gardens. And so he came for me to, to be in, to sing in the show.

ctx.x: And had you worked, uh, in, uh, in the cafés before that?

No, I hadn't worked in, in the cafés before then. But, um, there was a fellow named, uh, uh, uh, uh. Wait a minute. I'll tell you in just a minute. He belongs to our club. Now, let's see. Uh, uh, uh, but anyway. Oh, my goodness. Why can't I think of that fellow's name? I'm so simple. I'm stupid. I just forget everything. Uh, uh, Clyde, uh, Clyde, Clyde Jenkins. Clyde Jenkins is his name, see. He heard me singing, and he heard the records. And he used to come to our house where we lived up there on, on, uh,…
I don't remember, uh, uh, uh, Jenkins as a musician. Clyde Jenkins. What was his instrument? He plays piano. He's still, uh, still active as a piano? He's still, he's still. I mean, he plays.
